evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant women reporting reduced fetal movements (RFM) after 24 weeks: confirming viability, CTG and ultrasound assessment, and follow-up. Verified against the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual (reduced fetal movement chapter, based on RCOG Green-top 57) and NICE NG201.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 12 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: RCOG Green-top 57 (cited by MOH) not opened directly

pathophysiology.summary: A reduction in fetal movements can be the first sign of fetal compromise — the fetus conserves energy by moving less when placental oxygen supply falls. Most episodes are benign, but missed compromise (for example growth restriction) can lead to stillbirth (MOH).
keyMechanisms: Placental insufficiency → fetal hypoxaemia → reduced movement as an adaptive response.
Growth restriction and reduced amniotic fluid often coexist (MOH links RFM with IUGR).
Movements are perceived from about 18–20 weeks; maternal perception varies with placental site and activity.

symptoms: Mother reports fewer or weaker movements than usual, or none.
Ask about bleeding, pain, fluid loss, previous episodes.
physicalSigns: Maternal observations; fundal height (small for dates).
redFlags: No fetal heart detected — urgent ultrasound
Small for gestational age or reduced liquor on ultrasound

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Small biometry, abnormal Doppler — see FGR topic.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: If present and no risk factors, reassure.

references.title: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Abnormal: reduced variability, decelerations, abnormal baseline.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Normal CTG → reassure; abnormal → obstetric review and further assessment.
ruleIn.normalValue: Baseline 110–160 beats/min, variability 5–25, accelerations, no decelerations

ruleOut.testName: Ultrasound — fetal biometry and amniotic fluid
ruleOut.modalityTarget: When RFM persists or risk factors present (MOH)
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Small for gestational age; reduced liquor.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: CTG plus liquor assessment approximates a biophysical profile (MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: Contact
actions: Women should contact maternity services any time of day or night with concerns after 24+0 weeks (NICE NG201).

clinicalManagement.title: 24–28 weeks
actions: Confirm the fetal heart by auscultation and reassure (MOH).

clinicalManagement.title: After 28 weeks
actions: CTG once; if normal, reassure — 70% of single RFM episodes are uncomplicated (MOH).
Ultrasound for growth and liquor if there is concern (small for dates, risk factors, recurrent RFM).
Abnormal CTG or ultrasound → obstetric review, manage as fetal compromise or growth restriction.

learningObjectives: Assess reduced fetal movements by gestation and identify fetal compromise.

references.title: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health
NICE NG229: Fetal monitoring in labour

keyPoints: Present the same day — do not wait.
Ultrasound if risk factors or recurrence.
pitfalls: Advising the woman to wait and count at home.
Reassuring without checking growth in recurrent RFM.
Mistaking maternal pulse for fetal heart.

patientEducation: Know your baby's usual pattern; report any reduction at once.
Do not use home Dopplers for reassurance.
mdtReferrals: Obstetric review for abnormal CTG, small fetus or recurrent RFM.
dischargeCriteria: Normal fetal heart/CTG and no concerns on ultrasound or risk assessment.
Woman knows to return immediately if movements reduce again.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Return immediately with any further reduction; recurrent RFM → growth scan and obstetric review.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Normal CTG and no risk factors

medicationPlan.note: No medicines are part of RFM assessment.

guidelineComparison.title: RFM assessment by gestation (MOH)
guidelineComparison.note: NICE NG201 advises contacting services at any time with concerns after 24+0 weeks and notes that structured awareness packages (AFFIRM) did not reduce stillbirth.
